newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - ABC's Padden upbeat on ad market.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ABC's Padden upbeat on ad market.

text.p: Preston Padden, the new president of Walt Disney Co's ABC television network, said Wednesday he was "optimistic" about the early advertising market after the network unveiled its fall schedule last week.

"We continue to have a very strong story, particularly with respect to delivering adults 18-49," Padden told Reuters in an interview. "My sense from the few conversations I've had with the agency community is that our new schedule was very well received."
All three networks presented their new fall lineups to advertisers last week.

Padden, noting the industry consensus that the upfront, or advance, market by advertisers was up over last year, made the usual pitch that major broadcast networks "are still the only place any advertiser can go to reach the volume of consumers we can deliver."

Padden, whose appointment is effective this week, replaces David Westin, now president of ABC News. Padden will be responsible for network sales, affiliate relations, broadcast operations and engineering and network communications.

Padden, who has spoken with most of the members of the board of affiliate ABC stations in the last few days, said relations with the network appear to be "very good. There seems to be a spirit of respect and goodwill between ABC and affiliates that I hope to maintain and build."

Affiliates are anxious to see how the fall schedule, put together by Jamie Tarses, the new president of ABC Entertainment, is received by viewers. The network's average audience has declined, knocking it into third place.
Padden, noting that Tarses will continue to report to ABC president Robert Iger, said he has no problem with the corporate structuring.

"To be honest, nobody has ever hired me for my creative programming ability," he said. "I expect to have plenty to do. Bob Iger is looking forward to me taking some of the business issues off his shoulders."
Padden said his first priority was to "take a zero-based look at the way the entire business operates, and try to put both the network and the affiliates on a firm foundation for the future."

Padden, who was chairman of American Sky Broadcasting, a satellite television joint venture between News Corp Ltd and MCI Communications Corp, said he has spent the last year and a half "immersed" in digital TV.
He said he hoped digital television could help "reinvent network television for the benefit of the network and affiliates...in the context of declining market share among the traditional networks."
"The first job is to help Bob Iger operate the business of the ABC television network as efficiently and effectively as we can," Padden said.
"The second is to help Bob come up with a plan to grow the ABC television network business in ways that position the network and the affiliates for the future of television," he added.
